script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for October 9. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Apple cores become soil that grows apple trees.  Death feeds life feeds death feeds life.  Composting isn't just rot—it's transformation.

In nature, there's no 'away' to throw things. Everything cycles. Leaves fall, decompose, become soil, feed trees, become leaves. Designing for closed loops eliminates waste entirely. Composting requires decomposers—bacteria, fungi, worms.  They do the work of transformation.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Nothing is truly wasted in closed loops.  What one process discards, another needs.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Loop Closure - What Waste Could Become Input?.

Here's your activity: What do you discard that could become input elsewhere? Failed projects contain lessons. Ended relationships contain wisdom. Old skills have new applications. How can you compost your 'waste' into nutrients for new growth? This helps you identify opportunities to close loops and eliminate waste.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about food becoming soil can be applied to loop closure - what waste could become input?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
